source: v2 Study A (data/runs/20261011_v2A_{sol,opus,fable}.jsonl), 30 tournaments; numbers from bench/v2report.ts (styles_raw.json has the v1 vs v2 rows)

models.style: Loose-aggressive and format-aware, as in v1. Opens about half its hands and raises 30% preflop. With under 15 big blinds it shoves 33% of the time (v1: 32%). Talks much less than in v1 (9% of decisions, was 33%). Almost never cites earlier hands.

The most aggressive seat: VPIP 67, PFR 46, shoves 37% of short-stack spots, and uses the free raise amount on 13% of its decisions. It reads the payout structure: 9% of its reasoning mentions the bubble or the money, the most of any model, though it once thought it was still on the bubble three-handed when three were paid. Talks on 89% of decisions.

Solid on paper (VPIP 48, PFR 30) and the heaviest user of memory: 14% of its reasoning cites what opponents did in earlier hands ('Jev is a calling station'). It talks on 95% of decisions. It lost chips to Haiku and Luna and often reached the late levels short, then shoved. Its losses aren't all-in luck: the all-in adjustment moves it 0.6 bb/100.

No longer the river folder. At effort low (v1: none) it raises twice as often preflop (PFR 27 vs 13), shoves 15% short-stacked (v1: 0.7%), folds 48% to river bets (v1: 74%), and gave up the winner on 5 of 13 heads-up river folds (v1: 23 of 50). It was the best of the cheap seats, with the most wins.

Unchanged at heart: plays 70% of hands, never shoves short (0 of 99 spots), talks on 84% of decisions, and still misreads its hand. 40 of 50 'I have a set' claims were wrong, despite cards now being spelled out in words. Now that it has memory, 16% of its reasoning cites opponents' past play. Results swing by table: +146 bb/100 at Fable's table, −285 at Opus's.

Looser than in v1 (VPIP 47 vs 31, PFR 20 vs 6) with the bigger menu and the payout sheet, but still a near break-even middle finisher. It bets a third of the pot after the flop more than anything else.
Still the table's donor: last or near last everywhere (−146 bb/100, no wins in 30). It calls a lot and raises preflop only 6% of the time. After the flop it bets half pot or moves all-in.
